_about: Bomber hit rates on ships by kind (release 2; the design director's rulings of 22 November 2026 18:13Z and 18:27Z on the historian's counts, /mnt/project-files/historian/bomber-hit-rates-ships-1122.md; the form at air-battles/hitrates/form-hit-rates-by-kind.md). src/campaign/hitrates.ts. With the switch on, a strike on ships no longer counts the law's single 0.04 a bomber times its crews' naval skill, nor the spoil, nor the harbour's x1.5 and a surprise's x3: each bomber that released is worth its kind's rate for its navy, by whether fighters were over the ships ('covered') or not ('open'). 'underWay' holds each navy's own counted rows; a navy without a row takes its senior partner's ('kin'), then 'pool' (the rows pooled across the navies counted, D). 'anchor': ships at anchor, the rows that were the surprises (Taranto 0.55 and Pearl 0.72 a torpedo, their middle 0.64; Pearl's armour-piercing bombs 0.175, D); a dive bomber at anchor is its row under way times 'diveTimes' (today's harbour factor, a knob). 'fixed': the month (turn) from which a navy's own row gives way to the pool (America's torpedoes after the Mk 13's faults were cured: the historian's month; null until then, so its 1942 row of 0 stands). 'land': a land bomber group's kinds by nation, rows of [from turn, dive share, torpedo share], the rest level (Ju 87 dive; KG 26, SM.79, Nell, Betty and Beaufort torpedo): the historian's shares, none of ours meanwhile, so every land group is level until they come. 'mast': mast-height attacks (Bismarck Sea, wartime claims, L), only where the field has that attack: it has none today. 'on' is the switch for a new grand campaign; it cannot ship on until 'sourced' (the land shares and the Mk 13 month).
_pool: D, from the historian's rows. Dive, open: Japan's alone (Cornwall 8 of 16, Sims 3 of 4) = 0.55. Dive, covered: Japan 3 of 33, America 11.5 of 76 (Midway's carrier SBDs 8.5 of 48, Shokaku 3 of 28), Germany about 6 of 30 (Illustrious) = 20.5 of 139 = 0.15. Torpedo, without America's 1942 drops (a weapon's fault, not its crews; Q4): Kates 2 of 13 and Nells 0 of 12 = 2 of 25 = 0.08, one row until the historian counts torpedoes with no fighters overhead (Prince of Wales and Repulse). Level at sea: 0 (Midway's 320 bombs, Coral Sea's hundred). Mast height: 0.5 a bomb (Bismarck Sea, L).
